## Two Pollutants, Different Rules in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the EPA’s Acid Rain Program used different mechanisms for sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. In the sulfur dioxide system, an allowance represented permission to emit one ton. Allowances operated within an aggregate cap, with trading among covered sources.

The sulfur dioxide program expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 emissions units at 110 plants. Substitution or compensating units brought the Phase I total to 445 units, and Phase II began in 2000. The program’s final cap, set in 2010, was 8.95 million tons—a permitted total, not a measure of actual emissions.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a separate timeline and approach. It began in 1996 and used rate-based requirements for certain coal-fired units, without a cap or allowance trading. The two pollutants were therefore governed by different rules and timelines.
